chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Drummers' respect among other musicians
summary: DeMichael says drummers are not comedians and took up vibes to overcome the image; Saunders says it takes time to live down.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And, again, this is what I was talking about earlier. The drummer being accepted as a musician by the other musicians, like, drum soloists, there's a time to talk and there's a time to get off the stand and have a drink.
Right, get off the stand and have a drink, right, no, no, right, right.
And I had to train some very experienced musicians.
Yeah, right, right.
Don't do that.
Just to undertake three chorus es or whatever, right.
Right, and come back in, and don't come back in --
Right, right.
You either (unintelligible) change keys when you came back in and then tell me you're going to change keys.
Right, right.
That would throw me (unintelligible).
Right, right, right, right, right.
But it's -- I'm sure all drummers have felt this, that they're not comedians.

Right. Well, that's true, too, that's true. But, see, it's just like anything else. It's just a thing that happened years ago that you have to live down, and you're not going to live it down in two or three days. It's going to take time, a lot of time, for it to live down.
That's why it's good to see somebody like Louie Bellson, who likes beautiful arrangements, too.
Right, right.
But they're looked upon as exceptions. That's one reason I took up vibes. To try to overcome that.
Yeah.
That's a very sore point with me.

Right, right. Well, see, where your musical knowledge is extended, you would be more offensive than another guy with less musical ability. He -- maybe he wouldn't even pick up on that particular point. But through the knowledge that you have of music and all of that, and this guy really -- I mean, you can read anything that he reads, so who are you putting on, you know? Right.
